findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update()` called but `prisma` is never imported (imports end at line 20) — type-check failure and a hard `ReferenceError` on every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97-100 — `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the zod `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper, not `.data`; it is written straight to `credential.key`, so stored Google credentials become `{success:true,data:{…}}`. Next load's `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` throws — permanent, silent breakage on the *normal* (non-sync) path

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 — `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, both of which stringify to `"[object Object]"` — the second overwrites the first. Effective schema is `{access_token: string}` and zod's default strip discards `refresh_token`, expiry, `instance_url`, `scope`. The "any numeric property is the expiry" comment describes behavior that does not exist. A gate that goes green while validating nothing

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27 — Missing `refresh_token` is replaced with the literal sentinel string `"refresh_token"`, applied unconditionally (the sync-mode check at line 15 is not reused). Callers persist it verbatim (`office365calendar:264`, `office365video:93`). Real refresh tokens are overwritten; the next refresh sends `refresh_token=refresh_token` → `invalid_grant` → permanent disconnect requiring full re-auth

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15` vs `:18 — Return type is branch-dependent: sync mode returns a raw `fetch` `Response`; fallback returns the provider-specific shape. Typed `() => any`, so nothing catches it. `googlecalendar:94` does `res?.data` (undefined → TypeError, swallowed by the non-`invalid_grant` catch → returns stale auth); `hubspot:192` reads `.expiresIn` → `NaN` and writes the `Response` itself as `key` inside a log-only catch. The feature this PR ships is broken for Google and HubSpot with zero signal

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-57 — The `state.teamId` branch checks only accepted *membership*, creates the team credential, and returns at line 56 — `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam` (line 59) is unreachable for team flows and is called with `teamId: null` otherwise. `state` is attacker-supplied (`decodeOAuthState` just `JSON.parse`s `req.query.state`), so any ordinary member can craft `state={"teamId":N}` and write team-wide credentials — including Stripe payout destination

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — Auth is `req.headers[name] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If the secret is unset, both sides are `undefined` and the check **passes for a request with no header at all** — the guard goes green precisely when the secret is missing. Non-constant-time; header name not lowercased (Node lowercases inbound keys); array-valued duplicate headers never match. This is the only authentication on a public route that writes OAuth credentials for arbitrary `userId`

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101-107 — The freshly refreshed token is persisted to the DB but the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token` / `instance_url` — the refresh buys nothing for the request that paid for it

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 — Unconditional refresh-token grant on **every** service construction (called from the constructor) — no expiry check, no timeout, no cache, no locking. Adds a synchronous `login.salesforce.com` round-trip to every booking/availability path, churns Salesforce token limits, and concurrent bookings race to write `credential.key` (lost update)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `response.statusText !== "OK"` used as the success check — `statusText` is empty under HTTP/2 and undici, and is `"Created"`/`"No Content"` for other 2xx. Successful refreshes throw `HttpError` with an empty message; a 200 with an error body passes. Should be `!response.ok`

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96-99 — Credential overwritten with `{...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token}`; under sharing mode `data` is `{access_token}` only, erasing `instance_url`, `id`, `issued_at`, `signature`, `scope`, `token_type`. Next construction points jsforce at `undefined` — permanent breakage from a path whose only visible outcome was "refresh succeeded"

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-14 — Sync-endpoint `fetch` has no timeout/`AbortSignal`, no `response.ok` check, no retry, no auth header or signature, no `Content-Type`. Node fetch has no default timeout, so a hung self-hosted endpoint blocks a booking indefinitely; a 5xx or HTML error page is passed downstream to `handleErrorsJson`/`handleLarkError` and misreported as a token-parse failure

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 — The outbound leg sends only `calcomUserId` + `appSlug` with **no authentication**, over an unvalidated URL (no https enforcement), and the response is trusted and persisted as credentials. The documented contract asks self-hosters to expose an unauthenticated endpoint returning live access tokens keyed by an integer id — trivially enumerable; MITM injects tokens straight into the credential table

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — The entire sync response replaces `credential.key`, but the PR's own contract says the endpoint returns only access token + expiry — the stored `refresh_token` is deleted on first sync refresh. MS Teams disconnects permanently once the access token expires, far in time from the cause

webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:88`, `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:84`, `office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:77 — Switched to `refreshOAuthTokens` but **not** to `parseRefreshTokenResponse` — they still validate strict app-specific shapes (Webex requires `refresh_token` + `refresh_token_expires_in`; Lark requires a `data.data.{…}` envelope; Teams reads `expires_in`). On the sync path all three fail or compute immediate expiry. The feature is wired into only 3 of 8 refresh sites coherently

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `schema.parse()` (not `safeParse`) throws an uncaught `ZodError` → 500 with a body shape unlike every other branch's `{message}`. External integrators can't distinguish "my payload is wrong" from "Cal.com is down", and 5xx retry logic will hammer the endpoint

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-264 — The diagnostic `console.error(…zodError…, "MS response:", responseJson)` was **deleted** and the helper now throws a bare generic message. On-call loses the only signal identifying which field Microsoft returned wrong. Behavior also flipped from degrade-gracefully to throw-into-booking-paths

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23 — `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` discards the zod issue list, the app slug, and the credential id. The identical string is thrown from Google, Office365 and Salesforce paths — a support ticket can't be traced to a field or a provider

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61-92 — `findFirst` matches on `userId`+`appId` only — no `teamId` filter, no `orderBy`, no duplicate handling — so with multiple accounts for one app it clobbers an arbitrary row. The update path never resets `invalid` to `false`, so a successful re-sync silently doesn't take effect. Non-atomic find-then-write races on concurrent webhooks

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:243-281 — In sync mode expiry is stripped (finding 3) and never advanced, so `isExpired`/`getToken` sees an expired credential on **every** call → a token round-trip per calendar operation against the self-hoster's endpoint. Unbounded request amplification under load

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5-12` & `decodeOAuthState.ts:5-12 — `encodeOAuthState` `JSON.parse`s then immediately `JSON.stringify`s — a no-op returning its own input, byte-identical to `decodeOAuthState` but for the last line, and named backwards. It creates the false impression that state is encoded/signed at a CSRF-relevant boundary
`encodeOAuthState.ts` / `decodeOAuthState.ts` (both)

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — `appConfig.slug` in the OAuth `redirect_uri` replaced with a hardcoded `"zoho-bigin"` while lines 12 and 22 still read `appConfig.slug`/`appConfig.scope`. A slug rename now produces a mismatched `redirect_uri` (opaque Zoho error) instead of a lookup failure; the template literal no longer interpolates anything

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:20,28,52-54 — Error-shape inconsistency on a new external contract: config-disabled and auth-failure both return 403; three different "not found" strings; success returns interpolated prose with no machine-readable field; no route versioning

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:57 — `this.conn = this.getClient(credential).then(...)` is assigned in the constructor, and `getClient` can now reject (network error, `HttpError`, helper throw). No rejection handler is attached at construction; previously `getClient` did no I/O, so this risk is new — an unawaited instance yields `unhandledRejection`

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:6 — Imports its own sibling as `"../oauth/decodeOAuthState"` instead of `"./decodeOAuthState"` — leftover from the file move

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` used verbatim; Node lowercases inbound header keys, so a non-lowercase configured value never matches. Fails closed *unless* the secret is also unset, in which case it composes with finding 7 to fail **open**

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` used verbatim; Node lowercases inbound header keys, so a non-lowercase configured value never matches. Fails closed *unless* the secret is also unset, in which case it composes with finding 7 to fail **open**

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` the header is accessed as `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` without normalizing the configured name. In Node/Next.js, `req.headers` keys are lowercased, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is set to any non-lowercase value (e.g., `Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), the lookup will return `undefined` even if the client sends the correct header, causing the secret check to fail (403). Additionally, if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (i.e., `undefined`), then `undefined !== undefined` is false and the check would incorrectly pass when the header lookup also returns `undefined` (fail-open on misconfiguration).
